Here’s a concise, fully integrated 12-week plan tailored for your client: 36-year-old recreational lifter with a right medial meniscus tear, cleared for low-impact strength only (no jumping or deep knee flexion under load). Objective: build strength and tissue tolerance safely, restore skiing readiness, and maintain or improve functional movement without knee flare-ups. The program combines three weekly strength sessions, two knee-friendly cardio days with progressively increasing load (weeks 4–8), a peak microcycle (weeks 10–12), and a comprehensive recovery/mobility plan.

Overall structure
- Phases: 3 Phases of 4 weeks each.
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and safe loading; establish technique, ROM, tendon tolerance.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload on strength with increased cardio volume and conditioning density.
  - Phase 3 / Peak (Weeks 9–12): Strength consolidation, peak strength readiness, ski-specific readiness, and a controlled deload/testing window in Week 12.
- Weekly cadence:
  - Strength: 3 days (A / B / C) on non-consecutive days (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri).
  - Cardio: 2 days (Cardio 1 and Cardio 2) on non-strength days or after lighter sessions; knee-friendly modalities only.
  - Optional mobility/recovery days: 0–2 days per week.
- Daily structure: 3–4 core lifts per strength session; emphasis on safe ROM, slow tempo, and controlled loading. Cardio sessions emphasize endurance and conditioning without knee strain. Recovery/mobility integrated daily.

Phase 1: Foundation and safe loading (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: establish knee-friendly strength base, improve quadriceps/hip/arthrokinematics, tendon tolerance, and reintroduce squat patterns with safe ROM.

Weekly pattern (repeat A/B/C across weeks, adjust per cues)
- Week 1
  - A (Lower Body Strength, safe ROM)
    1) Goblet Squat or light DB Front Squat — 3x10–12, tempo 3-1-1-0
    2) Leg Press (shallow depth) — 3x12, tempo 3-0-1-0
    3) Romanian Deadlift with DBs — 3x10, tempo 3-0-1-0
    4) Seated Hip Abduction/Adduction — 3x12 each side
    5) Calf Raise (on Leg Press) — 3x15
  - B (Upper Body Push/Pull)
    1) Seated DB Shoulder Press — 3x10
    2) Lat Pulldown (neutral grip) — 3x10–12
    3) Dumbbell Floor Press or DB Bench Press — 3x10
    4) Cable Row — 3x12
    5) Plank or Side Plank — 3x30–45s
  - C (Single-leg/Balance and gait)
    1) Split Squat to Box (shallow depth) — 3x8 per leg
    2) Step-up to low/raised surface — 3x10 per leg
    3) Glute Bridge — 3x15
    4) Pallof Press — 3x12 per side
    5) Farmer’s Carry — 3x40–60s

- Week 2
  - A: Goblet Squat 4x8–10; Leg Press 3x12; Romanian Deadlift 3x10; Hip Abduction 3x12; Calf Raise 3x15
  - B: Seated DB OHP; Lat Pulldown; Floor Press; Seated Row; Suitcase Carry
  - C: Bulgarian Split Squat (bench-supported) 3x8; Lateral Band Walks 3x20 steps; Glute Bridge March 3x12 per leg; Pallof Press 3x12; Farmer’s Carry 3x45–60s

- Week 3
  - A: Goblet Squat 4x6–8; Leg Press 3x10; Hip hinge (Romanian/Trap Bar) 3x8; Hip Thrust 3x10; Calf Raise 3x15
  - B: DB Shoulder Press; Seated Cable Row; Incline DB Press; Lat Pulldown; Curl-to-Press (optional) 2x12
  - C: Split Squat to Box 3x8; Step-up to Box 3x8; Glute Bridge w/ Abduction 3x12; Farmer’s Carry 3x40–60s

- Week 4
  - A: Goblet Squat (deeper if tolerated) 4x8; Leg Press 3x12; Romanian Deadlift 3x8–10; Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge 3x12; Calf Raise 3x15
  - B: DB OHP or Dumbbell Floor Press; Seated Row; Push-ups (incline if needed) 3x10–12; Face Pulls 3x12; Pallof Press 3x12
  - C: Bulgarian Split Squat (shallow) 3x8; Lateral Band Walks 3x20; Glute Bridge with March 3x12 per leg; Farmer’s Carry 3x45–60s

Phase 2: Build strength tolerance and conditioning up (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: increase absolute strength with higher loads, maintain knee ROM, and increment cardio conditioning volume.

Structure: Maintain A/B/C but gradually push loading; two cardio days per week (Cardio 1 and Cardio 2) with progressive volume and complexity.

Week 5
- A: Front Squat (DB) 4x6–8; Leg Press 3x12; Romanian Deadlift 3x8–10; Hip Thrust 3x10–12; Calf Raise 3x15
- B: DB Floor Press or DB Bench Press 3x8–10; Seated Cable Row 3x10–12; DB Lateral Raise 3x12; Lat Pulldown 3x10–12; Core: dead bug or anti-extension 3x12 per side
- C: Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8 per leg; Walking Lunge short step 3x8 per leg; Glute Bridge with Band 3x12; Pallof Press 3x12; Farmer’s Carry 3x50–70s

Week 6
- A: Front Squat (DB) 4x6–8; Leg Press 3x10–12; Romanian Deadlift 3x8; Hip Thrust 3x12; Calf Raise 3x15
- B: Seated DB Shoulder Press 3x8–10; Barbell/DB Row 3x10; Incline DB Press 3x8–10; Face Pulls 3x12; Anti-Rotation Pallof 3x12
- C: Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8 per leg; Walking Lunge 3x8 per leg; Glute Bridge with Band 3x12; Farmer’s Carry 3x50–70s

Week 7
- A: Front Squat (DB) 4x6; Leg Press 3x10; Romanian Deadlift 3x8; Hip Thrust 3x12; Calf Raise 3x15
- B: DB Push Press (strict) 3x8–10; Seated Cable Row 3x10–12; Flyes or Floor Press 3x8–10; Lat Pulldown 3x10–12; Core: Pallof 3x12
- C: Split Squat to Box 3x8; Step-up to Box 3x8; Glute Bridge with Band 3x12; Farmer’s Carry 3x50–70s

Week 8

- B: DB Overhead Press 3x8–10; Bent-Over Row 3x10–12; Incline DB Press 3x8–10; Face Pulls 3x12; Pallof 3x12
- C: Bulgarian Split Squat (shallow) 3x8; Lateral Band Walks 3x20; Glute Bridge March 3x12; Farmer’s Carry 3x60s

Phase 3 / Peak and ski-readiness (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: consolidate gains, peak strength with knee-safe loads, introduce skiing-relevant unilateral control, and conclude with a testing/deload window at Week 12.

Week 9
- A: Front Squat (DB) 4x5–6; Leg Press 3x8–10; Romanian Deadlift 3x6–8; Hip Thrust 3x10; Calf Raise 3x12–15
- B: Floor Press or DB Floor Press 3x8–10; Seated Row 3x10–12; DB Shoulder Press 3x8–10; Lat Pulldown 3x10–12; Core: Pallof 3x12
- C: Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8 per leg; Step-Up to Box 3x8 per leg; Glute Bridge with Band 3x12; Farmer’s Carry 3x60s

Week 10

- B: Push-Ups or Floor Press 3x8–10; Barbell/DB Row 3x8–10; DB Overhead Press 3x6–8; Lat Pulldown 3x10–12; Anti-Rotation 3x12
- C: Split Squat 3x6–8 per leg; Step-Up Progression 3x6–8; Glute Bridge with Band 3x12; Farmer’s Carry 3x60–75s

Week 11
- A: Box Squat or Front Squat (DB) 4x4–5; Leg Press 3x6–8; Romanian Deadlift 3x6; Hip Thrust 3x8–10; Calf Raise 3x12
- B: DB Push Press 3x8–10; Barbell Row 3x8–10; Floor Press 3x6–8; Lat Pulldown 3x8–10; Anti-Rotation 3x12
- C: Split Squat 3x6–8 per leg; Step-Up 3x6–8; Glute Bridge with Band 3x12; Farmer’s Carry 3x60–75s

Week 12 (deload/testing window)
- A: Light technique and strength consolidation
  - Front Squat (DB) 3x5; Leg Press 2x10; Romanian Deadlift 2x8; Hip Thrust 2x12; Calf Raise 2x12
- B: Floor Press 3x8; Seated Row 3x10; DB Shoulder Press 3x8; Lat Pulldown 3x10
- C: Split Squat or Bulgarian Split Squat 3x6; Glute Bridge Hold 3x30–45s; Farmer’s Carry 3x60s
- Optional: 1RM or rep-max testing on key lifts if pain-free and clinician-approved
- Cardio in Week 12: one short 20–25 minute tempo session; one light activation session 15–20 minutes to promote recovery

Cardio plan: Weeks 4–8 progression (summary)
- Week 4: Cardio 1 25–30 minutes intervals; Cardio 2 ~30 minutes tempo/circuit
- Week 5: Cardio 1 28–32 minutes; Cardio 2 33–36 minutes
- Week 6: Cardio 1 32–36 minutes; Cardio 2 28–34 minutes (circuit)
- Week 7: Cardio 1 32–38 minutes; Cardio 2 35–38 minutes (tempo blocks)
- Week 8: Cardio 1 34–40 minutes; Cardio 2 ~40 minutes (sustained tempo or mixed)

Recovery and mobility (daily and weekly)
- Daily 8–15 minute mobility/soft-tissue routine integrated into warm-ups or post-workouts:
  - Soft-tissue work: quads, calves, IT band, glutes
  - Hip and ankle mobility: hip flexor stretch, 90/90 hip, ankle dorsiflexion, thoracic rotation
  - Knee-friendly activations: quadriceps activation, TKEs, glute bridging variations
- Weekly dedicated mobility sessions (2–3 sessions, 15–25 minutes each)
  - Session A: hips/knees/ankles emphasis; adductor mobility; glute activation; pigeon/90/90
  - Session B: thoracic mobility; wall slides; thread-the-needle; single-leg balance with reach
  - Session C (optional): ankle mobility and patellofemoral tracking drills
- Soft-tissue options: foam roller, massage ball for targeted points; light pressure only
- Recovery modalities: ice for swelling if needed; compression sleeve during heavy days; sleep 7–9 hours; hydration and electrolytes
- Sleep and stress: maintain consistent sleep schedule; stress management strategies (breathing, short walks)

Nutrition alignment (maintain weight while supporting training)
- Baseline maintenance: roughly 2,800–2,900 kcal/day (adjust to weight changes)
- Protein: 1.9–2.2 g/kg/day (roughly 140–170 g for an 80–85 kg athlete), distributed 25–40 g per meal
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day; higher on heavier training days
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; more on cardio days
- Pre/post workout: 40–60 g carbs and 15–25 g protein pre-workout; 30–60 g carbs and 20–40 g protein post-workout
- Special notes: omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin D as needed; consider creatine 3–5 g/day for strength support

Supplements (optional)
- Protein powder for convenience
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day
- Vitamin D and omega-3s if deficient or dietary intake is low
- Glucosamine/chondroitin: discuss with clinician if knee joint health is a concern

Progression and safety guidelines
- Technique first; progression only with pain-free, controlled ROM
- Use RPE to guide intensity: Phase 1 RPE 5–7; Phase 2 RPE 7–8; Phase 3 RPE 7–8
- If knee pain or effusion increases, reduce ROM depth, cut volume, or revert to a safer week
- Deload or repeat weeks if needed; never push through sharp or intolerable knee pain
- Regular check-ins: weekly weight, training load, and symptom tracking; adjust plan as needed

- A one-page peak-week cheat sheet with explicit load targets and testing protocols
